Implementation: - Core rule implementation: src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts - File header explicitly ties to story: - `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` - `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION` - `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE` - Defines ESLint RuleModule with proper meta: - `type: "problem"` - `docs.description: "Require @story and @req annotations on code branches"` - `recommended: "error"` - `fixable: "code"` - `messages.missingAnnotation: "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}."` (clear, parameterized error message) - JSON schema for options: `branchTypes` is an array of unique strings, `additionalProperties: false`. - Branch handling in `create(context)`: - Calls `validateBranchTypes(context)` to either obtain a list of branch types or a RuleListener that reports configuration errors. - If a listener is returned, it is used directly (covers invalid config case). - Otherwise, iterates the list of branch types and registers handlers: - Each handler invokes `reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef)`. - Special-case for `SwitchCase` with `test == null` (default case) to skip annotation enforcement (explicit edge-case handling).
- Helper utilities: src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts - DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES (REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA, REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION): - `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES = ["IfStatement", "SwitchCase", "TryStatement", "CatchClause", "ForStatement", "ForOfStatement", "ForInStatement", "WhileStatement", "DoWhileStatement"] as const;` - JSDoc includes `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and `@req REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA`. - Configuration validation and scope control (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE): - `validateBranchTypes(context: Rule.RuleContext): BranchType[] | Rule.RuleListener`: - Reads `options.branchTypes` from `context.options[0]`. - Filters for invalid types by checking membership in DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES. - If any invalid types exist, returns a `Program` listener that reports each invalid value with message: - `Value "${t}" should be equal to one of the allowed values: ${DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES.join(", ")}` - If valid, returns the configured list; otherwise falls back to all DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES. - This matches the story's invalid-configuration behavior description. - Comment association (REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION, REQ-NESTED-HANDLING support via AST): - `gatherBranchCommentText(sourceCode, node)`: - For `SwitchCase`, scans up to 2 lines above for lines starting with `//` or `/*`, collecting them in order. This supports cases where there is a blank line before the case and comments appear above (edge-case handling indicated in story Implementation Notes). - For all other branch types, uses `sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node)` and maps each comment to its `.value`, joining into a single string. - This provides association between comments and the specific branch node. - Annotation parsing and missing-annotation detection (REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING): - `getBranchAnnotationInfo(sourceCode, node)` (internal): - Calls `gatherBranchCommentText`. - `missingStory = !/@story\b/.test(text);` - `missingReq = !/@req\b/.test(text);` - Computes `indent` from the start line's leading whitespace. - Computes `insertPos` via `sourceCode.getIndexFromLoc({ line: node.loc.start.line, column: 0 })`. - `reportMissingStory(context, node, { indent, insertPos, storyFixCountRef })`: - On first missing story in a file (tracked by `storyFixCountRef.count === 0`): - Reports with `messageId: "missingAnnotation"`, `data: { missing: "@story" }`. - Provides fixer inserting `"// @story .story.md\n"` at `insertPos` with proper indent. - Increments `storyFixCountRef.count`. - On subsequent missing story for other branches, reports without fixer. - `reportMissingReq(context, node, { indent, insertPos, missingStory })`: - If `missingStory` is false, supplies fixer inserting `"// @req \n"` above the branch. - If the story is also missing, only reports the error (no fixer), avoiding conflicting edits. - `reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef)`: - Gets `missingStory`, `missingReq`, `indent`, `insertPos` from `getBranchAnnotationInfo`. - Builds an `actions` array for story and req. - Iterates actions and executes reporting for each missing annotation. - This covers both annotations in a single pass per branch node.
- Plugin integration (rule wired into plugin and configs): - src/index.ts - `RULE_NAMES` includes `"require-branch-annotation"`, enabling dynamic require via: - `const mod = require(`./rules/${name}`); rules[name] = mod.default ?? mod;` - `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` includes: - `"traceability/require-branch-annotation": "error"` - Configs: - `configs = { recommended: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], strict: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()] }`, where `createTraceabilityFlatConfig()` uses `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES`. - Therefore this rule is activated by both recommended and strict config presets, satisfying "Rule integrated into plugin configuration presets" in Definition of Done.
- Tests for this story/rule (behavioral coverage and traceability): - tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts - Header explicitly references the story and requirements: - `Tests for: docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md, docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md` - `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` - `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION - Verify require-branch-annotation rule enforces branch annotations` - Uses `RuleTester` with `ecmaVersion: 2020`. - Valid test cases confirm correct behavior when annotations are present and configuration scope is used: - IfStatement: - Comments directly before: `// @story ...` and `// @req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION`. - ForStatement with block comments. - SwitchCase with inline comments. - Try/finally and CatchClause with annotations. - DoWhileStatement, ForOfStatement, ForInStatement, WhileStatement all covered. - Default case allowed without annotations (shows deliberate choice of branch significance for SwitchCase only, not DefaultClause). - Config-scoped enforcement: - Ignoring SwitchCase when `branchTypes: ["IfStatement"]`. - Enforcing IfStatement when it is in the configured list. - Invalid test cases verify detection and auto-fix behavior: - IfStatement without annotations: expects two errors (`@story` and `@req`) and auto-fix adding story above the `if`. - For loop with only story: expects missing `@req` error and auto-fix to insert `// @req `. - While with only `@req`: expects missing `@story` error and auto-fix to insert default `@story`. - SwitchCase without comments: expects both `@story` and `@req` and an output where a story line is inserted above the `case` label, using the SwitchCase comment scanning logic. - DoWhile, ForOf, ForIn, Try/Catch all have tests that verify missing annotation detection and suggested edits. - Configurable scope tests: - A `ForStatement` without annotations with `options: [{ branchTypes: ["ForStatement"] }]` yields missing `@story` and `@req` and an output that adds a `@story` annotation. - Additional RuleTester run specifically for invalid `branchTypes` configuration: - `options: [{ branchTypes: ["UnknownType"] }]` expects an error message matching `/should be equal to one of the allowed values/`, validating configuration error handling from `validateBranchTypes`.
- Documentation for the rule (docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md): - Tied to story and requirements: - `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` - `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION` - `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE` - Describes behavior: - "Ensures that significant code branches (if/else, switch cases, loops, try/catch) have `@story` and `@req` annotations for traceability." - Configuration section: - Documents `branchTypes` option, default list (matching DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES), and allowed values. - Documents error behavior for invalid branch type: `Value "InvalidType" should be equal to one of the allowed values.` (aligned with helper implementation). - Examples: - Correct example showing if-statement annotated with `@story` and `@req`. - Incorrect example showing missing annotations. - Invalid configuration example for invalid `branchTypes` value.

traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS are satisfied based on concrete evidence:
- Core Functionality: The `require-branch-annotation` rule detects significant code branches (if/else, try/catch, switch cases, and loops) missing `@story` or `@req` annotations, as shown by the invalid cases in tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts and the logic in reportMissingAnnotations/reportMissingStory/reportMissingReq. - Quality Standards: The rule is implemented as a standard ESLint RuleModule with proper meta, schema, and RuleTester tests. It uses simple AST traversal and minimal per-node work (basic regex and array operations), aligning with ESLint performance guidelines. - Integration: DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES cover all required branch types; the rule is integrated into src/index.ts via RULE_NAMES and TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES, and is active in both recommended and strict configs. The behavior works regardless of nesting because it listens directly on branch node types, and there is no depth-sensitive special casing that would break nested structures. - User Experience: Error messages are clear and specific: `Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.` with `missing` set to `"@story"` or `"@req"`, and tests confirm that both missing annotations are reported separately, with auto-fix suggestions for the first missing @story and for missing @req (when story is present). The configuration error message for invalid branchTypes is also explicit and matches the documented behavior. - Error Handling: Edge cases are handled, including default switch cases (explicitly skipped), SwitchCase comment association with preceding blank lines via PRE_COMMENT_OFFSET scanning, and invalid configuration detection via validateBranchTypes returning a Program listener that reports each bad value. Tests verify these behaviors, including the invalid branchTypes scenario. - Documentation: A dedicated rule documentation file describes behavior, configuration, default and allowed branch types, and includes correct/incorrect code examples and invalid config example. This documentation references the story and requirements directly.
Given the implemented rule, helpers, tests, plugin integration, and documentation, and with the full Jest test suite passing, the story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS is fully implemented and passes.
